subject: simple question about example in Blangiardo et al. 2012 paper

messages.author: 778bd0cef6c473fc
messages.subject: simple question about example in Blangiardo et al. 2012 paper
parts:
From Page 12 of Blangiardo et al. 2012, Spatial and Spatio-temporal models with INLA: “Finally, it could be interesting to evaluate the proportion of variance explained by the structured spatial component.”

 

The code accompanying the above statement is pasted in below. My simple question: I am confused as to what are the units on the variance terms, e.g., var.RRspatial and var.RRhet, below?

 

#Finally we obtain the proportion of variance explained by the spatially structured component

#upsilon, taking the structured effect upsilon and calculating the empirical variance.

#First we create a matrix with rows equal to the number of areas and 1000 columns.

#Then for each area we extract 1000 values from the corresponding marginal distribution of upsilon

#and finally we calculate the empirical variance. We also extract the expected value of the variance

#for the unstructured component and build the spatial fractional variance.

mat.marg<-matrix(NA, nrow=Nareas, ncol=1000)

m<-mod$marginals.random$ID

for (i in 1:Nareas){

  u<-m[[Nareas+i]]

  s<-inla.rmarginal(1000, u)

  mat.marg[i,]<-s}

var.RRspatial<-mean(apply(mat.marg, 2, sd))^2

var.RRhet<-inla.emarginal(function(x) 1/x,

                          mod$marginals.hyper$"Precision for ID (iid component)")

var.RRspatial/(var.RRspatial+var.RRhet)

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] simple question about example in Blangiardo et al. 2012 paper
parts:
The units of components of a general additive model with a link function aren't necessarily straightforward, but if it's a model with an identity link function, then the variances would have the square of the unit of the observations as unit.  Not sure if that's what you're asking about.

Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] simple question about example in Blangiardo et al. 2012 paper
parts:
In such models, I wouldn't necessarily assign a unit to the model components at all, but there are usually other possible interpretations.
For the Poisson case, the log-link means that each component gives (the log of) a multiplicative change in the response expectations. If you can imagine what the "unit" of the log of a relative change is, then the variance would have the square of that, but I would say that they are both unitless.
For the binomial logic-link case, it's harder to directly interpret, but there is a relation with log-odds-ratios, which again would be unitless.

Finn

On 7 Jun 2017, at 19:49, Mercedes Bravo <mercede...@gmail.com> wrote:

Thanks for the fast response. I guess I am interested in two particular contexts:
(1) a poisson model such as that used in the Blangiardo paper
(2) a binomial model with logit link.

In the above cases, is it not possible to say what the units on the variance are?
